title: U.S. House · California's 40th District
area: Western Riverside County and eastern Orange County, including Corona, Norco, and parts of La Habra and Yorba Linda.

context.text: This is a battleground race between two sitting Republican incumbents. Redistricting under Proposition 50, approved by voters in November 2025, drew Rep. Ken Calvert (previously representing the 41st District) and Rep. Young Kim (previously representing the 40th District) into the same new 40th District. Calvert represents an estimated 51% of the new district's population and Kim about 35%. Both advanced from the June 2, 2026 top-two primary, in which Calvert received 35% of the vote and Kim 21%, defeating six other candidates; no Democrat advanced.

Both campaigns have run negative advertisements. As of July 9, 2026, Calvert had been endorsed by gubernatorial candidate Steve Hilton, the California Republican Assembly, and the California Congress of Republicans; Kim had been endorsed by U.S. Rep. James Gallagher, state Senate Minority Leader Brian Jones, and Americans for Prosperity Action.

candidates.name: Ken Calvert
candidates.currentRole: U.S. Representative, previously for California's 41st District (since 1993)

summary.text: Ken Calvert is a sitting U.S. Representative first elected to Congress in 1992, now running in California's newly redrawn 40th District against fellow Republican incumbent Young Kim after redistricting placed them in the same district. He chairs the Defense subcommittee of the House Committee on Appropriations.

background.text: Born in Corona, California, in 1953; graduated from Corona High School in 1971, earned an associate degree from Chaffey College in 1973, and a bachelor's degree in economics from San Diego State University in 1975.
Owned a small business and worked as a restaurant manager before serving as chair of the Riverside County Republican Party and his election to Congress in 1992.

priorities.text: Campaigning on his legislative record, citing top ratings from Americans for Tax Reform, the U.S. Chamber of Commerce, the National Federation of Independent Businesses, the National Association of Manufacturers, and the 60 Plus Association, and highlighting his legislation creating the E-Verify employment-verification system and federal funding for transportation and environmental projects.
priorities.quote: Ken's legislative work has received top ratings from the Americans for Tax Reform, U.S. Chamber of Commerce, National Federation of Independent Businesses, National Association of Manufacturers, and the 60 Plus Association.

positions.summary: Voted for the Laken Riley Act requiring DHS to detain undocumented immigrants charged with or convicted of theft and other offenses, and said he voted for it to protect Americans from those who do not abide by the law.
positions.quote: I voted for the Laken Riley Act to protect Americans from violent criminals and those who have demonstrated time and time again that they cannot abide by our laws.

positions.summary: Said the Dobbs ruling correctly shifted abortion policy to Congress and the states, and said Congress should not allow abortion on-demand up until birth while also expanding support for pregnancy-prevention and crisis-pregnancy resources.
positions.quote: We should not react by enacting extreme policies that allow for abortion on-demand, up until the point of birth.

positions.summary: Voted for the Tax Cuts and Jobs Act, which lowered individual and corporate tax rates, and voted to extend the law's expiring tax cuts, saying doing so would prevent a large tax increase.
positions.quote: With the House passage of the Tax Cuts and Jobs Act we are on the verge of enacting the most pro-growth tax policy our country has seen in decades. Lower taxes, more jobs, and higher wages are on the way.

record.text: Chairs the Defense Subcommittee of the House Committee on Appropriations and also serves on its Energy and Water Development and Related Agencies subcommittee in the 119th Congress (2025–2026).
Authored legislation creating the E-Verify system used to check employees' legal work status, according to his campaign.

candidates.name: Young Kim
candidates.currentRole: U.S. Representative, previously for California's 40th District (since 2021)

summary.text: Young Kim is a sitting U.S. Representative first elected to Congress in 2020, now running in California's newly redrawn 40th District against fellow Republican incumbent Ken Calvert after redistricting placed them in the same district. She chairs the House Committee on Foreign Affairs.

background.text: Born in Incheon, South Korea, and lives in La Habra, California; earned a bachelor's degree in business administration from the University of Southern California in 1985.

Worked as director of community relations and Asian affairs for then-U.S. Representative Ed Royce and as a financial analyst before her election to Congress; represented District 65 in the California State Assembly from 2014 to 2016.

priorities.text: Campaigning on her record in Congress supporting President Trump's agenda and says she is working to reverse Biden-era policy on prices, crime, and border security.
priorities.quote: In Congress, I continue to fight every day to ensure President Trump has allies to undo the disastrous Joe Biden-Nancy Pelosi agenda that caused skyrocketing prices, rising crime, an open border, and a political class that serves the swamp instead of fighting for working families.

positions.summary: Says a single-payer approach is not the solution to healthcare costs and instead favors giving states more leverage over Medicaid and giving consumers more control over their coverage.
positions.quote: While I believe a one-size-fits-all single-payer approach to healthcare is not the solution, I am committed to working in Congress to ensure everyone has access to affordable high-quality healthcare and medical treatment.

positions.summary: Calls for securing the border and equipping Customs and Border Patrol with better technology, while also saying DACA recipients must be treated fairly and with compassion.
positions.quote: Any path towards immigration reform should ensure that our border and America's other points of entry are secure, and Customs and Border Patrol has the latest technology so they can effectively do their job. DACA recipients must also be treated fairly and with compassion and reforms must uphold American values and the rule of law.

positions.summary: Was an original cosponsor of a House resolution standing with Israel after the October 7, 2023 Hamas attack and spoke on the floor in support of Israel's right to defend itself.
positions.quote: Israel has a right to defend itself against terrorist aggression, bring its hostages home, and the right to exist.

record.text: Chairs the House Committee on Foreign Affairs and also serves on the House Select Committee on the Strategic Competition Between the United States and the Chinese Communist Party and the House Committee on Financial Services in the 119th Congress (2025–2026).
